rows.title: Man says Goldman Sachs put him through a gauntlet of 39 one-on-one interviews—and the decisive conversation was less than a minute
rows.standfirst: Goldman Sachs’ acceptance rate for internships is less than 1%.

rows.title: Bank of America CEO says he hired 2,000 recent Gen Z grads from 200,000 applications, and many are scared about the future
rows.standfirst: Brian Moynihan says the fears are understandable, but urges young grads not to lose hope about the job market.

rows.title: Britain’s Royal Family is hiring someone to write their letters: It’s based at Buckingham Palace, comes with free lunch, and pays $43,000 a year
rows.standfirst: The correspondence team drafts “bespoke responses that answer varying and often unique queries” on behalf of the Royal Family.

rows.title: Is Iran next for Trump? A currency collapse, energy crisis, and water shortage have exploded into unrest against the regime
rows.standfirst: On Friday, Trump warned that if Iran kills peaceful protesters, “the United States of America will come to their rescue. We are locked and loaded and ready to go.”

rows.title: Warren Buffett left his Berkshire Hathaway job with a parting lesson for young Gen Z workers: ‘Be very careful who you work with’
rows.standfirst: The prolific investor, entrepreneur, and Oracle of Omaha, Warren Buffett, advises young professionals to be selective about jobs and bosses—but not salaries.

rows.title: Ray Dalio says AI is in ‘the early stages of a bubble,’ so watch out for 2026
rows.standfirst: After strong returns in U.S. markets last year, 2026 might be a different story.

rows.title: NYC fights sale of bankrupt rentals after Mamdani blasts living conditions
rows.standfirst: City authorities on Monday asked a bankruptcy judge to delay a Chapter 11 auction scheduled for Thursday.

rows.title: Business leaders are growing more optimistic, JPMorgan survey finds
rows.standfirst: Almost two in five leaders at midsize businesses expressed optimism—especially about their own company’s future performance.

rows.title: Mamdani advisor under fire for resurfaced ‘white supremacy’ tweets but landlords are really upset about hearings ‘to shame and embarrass them’
rows.standfirst: Amir Korangy of The Real Deal told Fortune that Cea Weaver is “outranked by moderate Mamdani allies” and has no authority to seize buildings.

rows.title: ‘It feels challenging to break through’: Most recruiters say they can’t find talent while 80% of job seekers feel unprepared to find a job
rows.standfirst: “They’re navigating fierce competition, uncertain about which roles they qualify for, and wondering whether their AI skills measure up,” said Teuila Hanson, LinkedIn’s chief people officer.

rows.title: Top economist says latest jobs data shows a ‘jobless expansion’ with no historical precedent—and it’s ‘gut-wrenching’ for the middle class
rows.standfirst: “We’re growing, but we can’t generate jobs,” KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk told Fortune. “Never seen anything like it.”

rows.title: Americans missed out on a ‘once-in-a-lifetime’ chance to buy a house—the 3 shifts it would take to make housing affordable are ‘very unlikely’
rows.standfirst: “We see the housing market remaining relatively stuck without major progress being made on affordability,” home construction CEO says.

rows.title: Trump threatens to ban Wall Street from buying the house next door, saying ‘American Dream is increasingly out of reach for far too many people’
rows.standfirst: Trump has not yet released draft legislation or an executive order, but officials and outside analysts say the administration is exploring several avenues.

rows.title: AI layoffs are looking more and more like corporate fiction that’s masking a darker reality, Oxford Economics suggests
rows.standfirst: “Firms don’t appear to be replacing workers with AI on a significant scale,” the firm said. It suspects some are trying to “dress up layoffs” as good news.

rows.title: For jobless Gen Z, healthcare is the place to be as blue-collar hiring outstrips office jobs, says ADP’s top economist
rows.standfirst: ADP’s jobs report delivered a sucker-punch to Gen Z grads this week: While hiring is up across private payrolls according to December data, it was offset by a significant drop in professional and business services.

rows.title: 3 things Trump did in 24 hours to show that he’s in control of American business
rows.standfirst: “He’s taking an extreme left-wing position which looks like state capitalism,” said Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, a longtime corporate governance scholar and the founding dean of Yale’s Chief Executive Leadership Institute.

rows.title: Sluggish economy crawls on with 50,000 jobs added in December, unemployment ticks down to 4.4%
rows.standfirst: The data suggests that businesses are reluctant to add workers even as economic growth has picked up.

rows.title: Walmart’s CEO Doug McMillon out-earns the average American’s salary in less than 20 hours—during a typical 30-minute commute, he’s already made $1,563
rows.standfirst: Outgoing Walmart CEO Doug McMillon started out at the company making $6.50 hourly unloading trailers, and after four decades of climbing the ranks, he now fetches $75,000 every day.

rows.title: Men joined the labor force at three times the rate of women in 2025
rows.standfirst: December’s jobs report shows 91,000 women left the workforce while 10,000 men joined.

rows.title: An exec at $62 billion giant Colgate says Gen Z workers, despite getting flak for being woke and lazy, are actually ‘pushing us to get better’
rows.standfirst: Sally Massey, the chief human resources officer at the $62 billion giant Colgate-Palmolive, is hitting back that young staffers aren’t the career sloths some typecast them to be.

rows.title: A Supreme Court ruling that strikes down Trump’s tariffs would be the fastest way to revive the stalling job market, top economist says
rows.standfirst: Trade-exposed industries suffered steep losses last year. The manufacturing sector, for example, has hemorrhaged 70,000 jobs since April.

rows.title: Google’s Sergey Brin admits he’s hiring ‘tons’ of workers without degrees: ‘They just figure things out on their own in some weird corner’
rows.standfirst: Google cofounder Sergey Brin studied graduate computer science at Stanford—but admits Gen Z no longer needs a degree to land a high-paying job at the tech giant.

rows.title: ‘Something big’ just happened in the U.S. housing market, real estate CEO says. And it could mean the difference of being able to buy a home or not
rows.standfirst: “The dreaded mortgage rate ‘lock-in’ effect is fading,” said real estate investor and Reventure CEO Nick Gerli.

rows.title: Acquisition.com CEO says leaders ‘have it backwards’ when it comes to hiring: She says she hires for emotional intelligence over technical skills
rows.standfirst: Leila Hormozi shares the hiring advice she learned from the Ritz-Carlton.

rows.title: Just like during Great Recession-era job struggle, Gen Z graduates are pouring into education as Teach For America reports a 43% surge in new teachers
rows.standfirst: Teach for America’s recent hiring surge reflects Gen Zers wanting an “opportunity for purpose and responsibility at a time where many entry jobs feel uncertain or disconnected from impact.”

rows.title: Americans making more than $100,000 are quickly losing faith in the economy—and it’s a red flag for the white-collar job market
rows.standfirst: The country’s highest earners are getting in on the pessimism.

rows.title: The 4.9% mystery: U.S. economy sees productivity surge, but drivers remain an ‘open question,’ top economist says
rows.standfirst: “We believe much of the rise is cyclical,” Morgan Stanley economists noted in the report.

rows.title: Forget the K-shaped economy, market veteran Ed Yardeni says—instead, it’s boomers hoarding wealth while Gen Z struggles to build it
rows.standfirst: The “gen-shaped economy” is defined by baby boomers’ massive net worth.

rows.title: Buying a home is 150% more expensive than in 2019. But here’s why Trump’s plan to shut out institutional investors could raise costs even more
rows.standfirst: “Big investors have nothing to do with how the housing shortage got created,” says Ed Pinto, a leading housing expert.

rows.title: ‘Humans could go the way of horses’: Goldman calculated how bad the AI ‘job apocalypse’ will be—and its analysts were pleasantly surprised
rows.standfirst: “6-7% of jobs will be displaced over the adoption period,” they said.

rows.title: Why the $38 trillion national debt doomed Fed independence regardless of the Trump/Powell drama, top economist says
rows.standfirst: “The reason markets didn’t react more is because we already wrecked the independence of the Fed,” said Tyler Cowen, economist and blogger extraordinaire.

rows.title: Carhartt CEO says they always focused on blue-collar workers—but hipsters came anyway: ‘We welcome anyone … that wants to celebrate hard work’
rows.standfirst: “We don’t try to be everything to everybody,” Carhartt CEO Linda Hubbard told Fortune, as she announced a blue-collar partnership with Ford Philanthropy.

rows.title: The job market is broken, but Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is ‘fairly confident’ that AI will increase productivity and therefore, hiring—but there’s a catch
rows.standfirst: As Gen Z struggles to start their careers, Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang predicts “more hiring” is on the way—but only for workers who embrace AI.

rows.title: America’s $38 trillion national debt is so big the nearly $1 trillion interest payment will be larger than Medicare soon
rows.standfirst: The staggering math behind the rapid rise in interest due on our outsize debt.

rows.title: Desperate job seekers are abandoning the idea of a ‘dream job’—but an economist warns bosses about what could happen next
rows.standfirst: More than a quarter of new employees took a pay cut, showing that bosses hold the power.

rows.title: Economy is marginally improving but only because the rich are splurging on luxury items and holidays, the Fed says
rows.standfirst: The Minneapolis Fed said that while retailers catering to higher-end consumers reported increased sales, those targeted at middle and lower-end consumers are “getting pretty beat up.”

rows.title: America’s hottest job opening right now is in the NFL—no degree is required, you won’t be fixed to a desk and it pays up to $20 million
rows.standfirst: Nine NFL teams are hiring head coaches—roles that pay millions but demand long hours, constant travel, and intense public scrutiny.

rows.title: The wealthy kids of property-rich U.K. parents get the highest-paying jobs, especially sons—and new research has revealed why
rows.standfirst: For every $133,800 of extra property wealth their parents had, U.K.’s rich kids were $20,000 better off. They also have more access to high-paying jobs—with men standing to gain the most.

rows.title: In the AI economy, the ‘weirdness premium’ will set you apart. Lean into it, says expert on tech change economics
rows.standfirst: Brandeis economics professor Benjamin Shiller says the stranger you are, the more employable you’ll be. Just look at self-driving cars and kangaroos.

rows.title: Just when Wall Street and Corporate America were looking forward to a year without trade fears, the ‘Tariff King’ strikes again
rows.standfirst: Trump announced tariffs on eight NATO allies and said earlier in the week that countries that do business with Iran would be hit with a 25% duty.

rows.title: If you want to be financially independent at a young age, don’t buy a house, serial investor says. Home ownership is just an ‘expensive indulgence’
rows.standfirst: “Your mortgage is just the starting point,” said author JL Collins.

rows.title: An AI-generated version of Trump’s voice is used in ad that promises an ‘all new Fannie Mae’ to tackle housing affordability
rows.standfirst: Trump plans to talk about housing at his appearance at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, where world leaders and corporate executives meet this week.

rows.title: Half of veterans leave their first post-military jobs in less than a year, and spouses face sky-high unemployment—this CEO has a $500 million fix
rows.standfirst: USAA CEO Juan C. Andrade says some veterans lose “their sense of belonging” in transitioning to corporate jobs. The company hopes fellowships, mentorship, and policy advocacy can help them get back on their feet.

rows.title: Truck driving is among the best jobs to have right now, Indeed says—it pays $160,000, with no degree required
rows.standfirst: Job-seekers might even find more luck hitting the road than trying to get their foot in the door of corporate offices, a new Indeed report says.

rows.title: Americans aren’t paying for all of Trump’s tariffs—only 96% of them, study finds
rows.standfirst: Despite the Trump administration’s claims, exporters are cutting shipments to the U.S. rather than lowering prices.

rows.title: The U.S. debt now equals $229,000 per household—and a hefty tax hike looms as the most probable outcome
rows.standfirst: Spiraling interest payments—which grew from $352 billion in 2021 to $970 billion in 2025—put the debt train on an accelerated track.

rows.title: Ray Dalio warns that the monetary order is breaking down, leaving us with a terrible choice: ‘Do you print money or let a debt crisis happen?’
rows.standfirst: Dalio told Fortune that he’s looking back at 500 years of history to try and make sense of today and see what’s coming.

rows.title: Trump doesn’t want America to be ‘a nation of renters,’ but experts say at least one of his proposals may put homeownership more out of reach
rows.standfirst: Experts told Fortune Trump’s proposal allowing Americans to tap their 401(k) for down payments could inflate prices and leave Americans poorer in retirement.

rows.title: The rise of on-demand leadership in the AI economy
rows.standfirst: Companies are favoring experienced consultants over permanent roles as judgment becomes more valuable than execution.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon says government should have power to intervene in AI-driven mass layoffs
rows.standfirst: Companies are favoring experienced consultants over permanent roles as judgment becomes more valuable than execution.

rows.title: Welcome to the ‘skills mismatch economy’: The shift from roles to skills making your résumé—and your job title—meaningless
rows.standfirst: Wharton and Accenture partnered on a huge “skills index” that crunched data on 100 million job postings. They found a “striking and persistent disconnect.”

rows.title: Despite promises that AI will create more jobs, 1.2 million jobs were actually slashed last year—a grim throwback to losses from the 2008 financial crisis
rows.standfirst: The tech industry announced 155,000 job cuts in 2025, up 15% from the year before, as the sector implements AI “much more quickly than any other industry.”

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says he welcomes government ban on mass-firing people for AI: ‘We’re going to cure a lot of cancers’
rows.standfirst: As AI threatens jobs, Jamie Dimon joins Elon Musk and Sam Altman on the case for financially supporting workers who are at risk.

rows.title: ‘Some form of crisis is almost inevitable’: The $38 trillion national debt will soon be growing faster than the U.S. economy itself, watchdog warns
rows.standfirst: “The United States is deeply indebted, and its finances are on an unsustainable long-term trajectory,” says the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget.

rows.title: No ‘job apocalypse’: Goldman Sachs CEO denies the AI hiring nightmare is real
rows.standfirst: “Technology has been disrupting jobs, changing the way people work, destroying jobs … for decades,” David Solomon says.

rows.title: Michelle Obama says friendships are as important as college degrees, job titles, and salary: ‘You’ve got to be really smart and selective about who you let in’
rows.standfirst: The former first lady says it’s important to make new friends, but advises people to be picky about who they let stick around. Longtime duos, like Oprah Winfrey and Gayle King, prove that friendship is a powerful career tool.

rows.title: ‘Wake up, AI is for real.’ IMF chief warns of an AI ‘tsunami’ coming for young people and entry-level jobs
rows.standfirst: Kristalina Georgieva is worried about Gen Z and the middle class: “This is moving so fast, and yet we don’t know how to make it safe [and] inclusive.”

rows.title: CEOs at Davos were split on how bad the AI job wipeout will be
rows.standfirst: In over a dozen meetings with top executives, two main themes stood out.

rows.title: AI productivity gains are making the rich richer, and they’ll wipe out jobs—but the IMF chief sees a silver lining for low-wage workers
rows.standfirst: Kristalina Georgieva sees an economic spillover effect brewing.

rows.title: From $40 billion to $225 billion: Inside the Trump housing plan to radically change the mortgage bond buying plan
rows.standfirst: An email obtained by the AP reveals how Trump official Bill Pulte raised the caps on mortgage bond holdings at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

rows.title: Trump’s housing market plan contains a fatal flaw and multiple obstacles, Morgan Stanley says
rows.standfirst: “Affordability in U.S. housing is a tricky issue that lacks a silver bullet,” the bank said. Trump’s actions are only “modestly helpful” for affordability.

rows.title: After 40 years of climbing the ladder, Walmart’s CEO Doug McMillon is retiring—his top tip for Gen Z is that ‘life is too short’ to hate their jobs
rows.standfirst: From decades of experience climbing the ranks, outgoing Walmart CEO Doug McMillon advised Gen Z graduates to find a gig that “does not feel like work.”

rows.title: Ryan Serhant thinks the American Dream was just a ‘slogan created by banks,’ but it was really about FDR, the Great Depression, and an economic crisis
rows.standfirst: “It’s like student debt. Everyone needs to go to college. It was a device to create interest payments on student debt.”

rows.title: The billion-dollar storm? Economists debate how much activity Winter Storm Fern laid waste to
rows.standfirst: Economist Jacob Fooks says most estimates suggest severe weather events can cut GDP by 0.5% to 2% annually — $150 billion to $600 billion.

rows.title: Trump’s own Big Beautiful Bill could add $5.5 trillion to the deficit and help sabotage his plan to ‘grow out’ of the national debt crisis
rows.standfirst: Prior to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump’s “growth” math stood a chance of closing the gap. Now it’s much harder to see it working.

rows.title: Coming soon: a lost generation of employee talent?
rows.standfirst: Entry-level employees don’t stay entry-level forever.

rows.title: As AI wipes out desk jobs, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser says the company is training 175,000 employees to ‘reinvent themselves’ before their roles change forever
rows.standfirst: Instead of letting Citigroup’s employees fend for themselves, the $205 billion bank has provided workers with an AI training mandate.

rows.title: Inside the world of Rick Rieder, the $2.3 trillion insomniac who might soon run the Fed
rows.standfirst: Rick Rieder oversees roughly $2.3 trillion in fixed income at BlackRock. His obsession with risk has made him a market legend—and a surprise Fed chair contender.

rows.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s 20,000-word essay on how AI ‘will test’ humanity is a must-read—but more for his remedies than his warnings
rows.standfirst: Anthropic CEO calls for AI companies to steer customers away from firing workers, wealthy tech billionaires to give away their money, and government to tax AI-generated wealth.

rows.title: Fed favorite Rick Rieder manages a $2.4 trillion BlackRock portfolio—and knows more about the bond market than anyone in America
rows.standfirst: As he eyes the next Fed chair, nothing’s a bigger deal in Trump’s policy decisions than what makes the bond market thrive or tank.

rows.title: This millennial quit her corporate 9-to-5 to pet sit for $70 per day. She ended up richer because she lives rent-free and gets to travel the world
rows.standfirst: Thanks to pet sitting, 32-year-old Georgina Welsh travels the world, works half the hours, and still takes home as much as she did in her corporate job.

rows.title: Banning investors won’t fix America’s housing shortage
rows.standfirst: It is a perfect example of the adage: don’t just do something; stand there. Renters would be better off without this proposal.

rows.title: As AI automates roles and companies pull back hiring, Americans hit rock-bottom confidence in landing a job—and baby boomers fear they’re locked out
rows.standfirst: Americans without college degrees, those earning less than $100,000, and baby boomers over the age of 60 are the least optimistic about their job prospects.

rows.title: Fed holds rates at an unusual moment: Stocks at record highs, dollar under pressure, and Powell in the crosshairs
rows.standfirst: Two governors dissented in favor of a cut, including Christopher Waller, a top contender for the chairmanship to replace Powell.

rows.title: Kalshi maintains a ‘perfect forecast record’ in predicting Fed rate decisions, beating professional forecasters, study finds
rows.standfirst: The National Bureau of Economic Research study found the prediction site showed “statistically significant improvement” over the Fed funds futures forecast.

rows.title: Trump now says he’s actually not ‘a huge fan’ of letting Americans tap their 401(k)s to use for a down payment
rows.standfirst: “I’m so happy with the way 401(k)s are doing,” President Donald Trump said.

rows.title: Get used to the K-shaped economy. It’s likely here until 2035, thanks to AI’s outsize benefit for the wealthy
rows.standfirst: “Eventually, it might bring things together, but in the meantime…it’s unlikely that AI helps at all with the K-shaped economy,” Innes McFee, CEO of Oxford Economics, tells Fortune in an exclusive interview.

rows.title: Jerome Powell got a direct question about the U.S. ‘losing credibility’ and the soaring price of gold and silver. He punted
rows.standfirst: Gold is up 84% year over year, and silver by a stunning 245%, but the Fed chair is looking elsewhere.

rows.title: Sergey Brin makes his biggest donation ever to tackle California’s housing crisis, weeks after moving to the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe
rows.standfirst: Weeks ago, the Google cofounder moved to a $42 million mansion on the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe. But he’s concerned about housing across the border.

rows.title: Struggling to remain relevant during the AI watercooler chat? Talk about your latest ‘new collar’ hire
rows.standfirst: LinkedIn’s Sue Duke says the AI-driven economy is already creating jobs and skills we’ve never seen before.

rows.title: Meet Trump’s next Fed Chair Kevin Warsh: He wants a back-seat central bank, a more bullish monetary policy, and for his dog to live a really long time
rows.standfirst: Trump confirmed Warsh as the Fed chair nominee Friday morning. Here’s what might be in store for the central bank.

rows.title: The new Fed chair’s billionaire father-in-law is a friend of Trump’s from college and has business interests in Greenland
rows.standfirst: Trump’s pick of Kevin Warsh pairs an inflation hawk with a deep Trumpworld connection through Ronald Lauder, a friend to the president for 60 years.

rows.title: Trump’s unlikely promise to ‘end inflation’ still saw families paying an extra $2,120 for goods and services in 2025
rows.standfirst: Exclusive: The year-on-year inflation increase equates to an added cost of $2,120 per household, assuming they purchased the same goods and services in 2025 that they bought in 2024. That includes an increase of $123 on electricity bills and $150 on groceries.

rows.title: ‘I just don’t have a good feeling about this’: Top economist Claudia Sahm says the economy quietly shifted and everyone’s now looking at the wrong alarm
rows.standfirst: EXCLUSIVE: The creator of the Sahm Rule on why she’s concerned about the long-term health of America’s economy.

rows.title: Kevin Warsh will inherit a challenge no Fed chief has faced since post-World War II regarding the spiraling $31 trillion national debt
rows.standfirst: Debt and deficits will put Kevin Warsh under great pressure to keep interest rates low and rely on short term borrowing. But long term that will have serious consequences.

rows.title: Ryan Serhant starts work at 4:30 a.m.—he says most people don’t achieve their dreams because ‘what they really want is just to be lazy’
rows.standfirst: Real estate mogul Ryan Serhant wakes up before the sun and values every minute like $1. He says most people struggle with work-life balance because they “lie to themselves.”

rows.title: ‘That’s exactly what a sock puppet does’: Elizabeth Warren accuses Kevin Warsh of softening his rate stance for Trump
rows.standfirst: “If Donald Trump says it, then Kevin Warsh echoes it, even though it contradicts everything he had done for years.”

rows.title: Ford CEO has 5,000 open mechanic jobs with up to 6-figure salaries from the shortage of manually skilled workers: ‘We are in trouble in our country’
rows.standfirst: “We do not have trade schools. We are not investing in educating a next generation of people,” Jim Farley said.
